blocks.etymology: Coined in analogy to wide open.

examples: He is usually a perspicuous man, but when it comes to that one issue, he has his eyes wide shut.
wiktionary.gloss: Deliberately closed (off). (figurative) Wilfully closed-minded; unwilling to see the truth.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English wresten, wrasten, wræsten, from Old English wrǣstan (“to twist forcibly, wrench”), from Proto-Germanic *wraistijaną, (compare Proto-Germanic *wrīhaną (“to turn, wind; to cover, envelop”), *wrīþaną (“to weave, twist”), Old Norse reista (“to bend, twist”)), from a derivative of Proto-Indo-European *wreiḱ-, *wreyḱ- (“to bend, twist”), *wreyt- (“to bend”). See also writhe, wry. The noun is derived from the verb.

senses.definition: to take power, control, or an object from someone with a lot of effort or force

examples.en: They managed to wrest control of the company from the founder.
examples.vi: Họ đã xoay xở giành quyền kiểm soát công ty từ tay người sáng lập.

senses.definition: to pull something away from someone violently using your hands

examples.en: He wrested the knife from the attacker's hand.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đã giật lấy con dao khỏi tay kẻ tấn công.

senses.definition: to change the true meaning of facts or words so that they suit your purpose

examples.en: His words were wrested to support an opposing view.
examples.vi: Lời nói của ông ấy đã bị bóp méo để ủng hộ một quan điểm đối lập.

senses.vi: xuyên tạc, bóp méo; làm sai lệch

thesaurus.definition: obtain by seizing forcibly or violently, also metaphorically

vi_block: Cố moi ra, cố rút ra.
Làm sai, làm trệch (nghĩa một từ); xuyên tạc, bóp méo (sự thật... ).

wiktionary.gloss: To pull or twist violently.

examples: He wrested the remote control from my grasp and changed the channel.
